external_primary_sources.claim_scope: EXIT reports that independent selection without contextual dependencies is weaker than context-aware extraction; this supports testing whether title-and-score-only selection loses semantic discrimination.
ECoRAG separates evidentiality from generic relevance and checks evidence sufficiency before further retrieval; this supports sufficiency and entailment controls rather than lexical admission alone.
HopRAG reports that lexical or semantic similarity can miss logical relevance; this directly motivates paraphrase, causal and multi-hop false-rejection probes for the hard lexical gate.
This primary study shows benchmark performance can be inflated when generated intermediate text contains ground-truth information; it supports explicit channel-leakage and held-out controls.

hypotheses.claim: With excerpts removed before selection, answer-level gains should now depend on text materialized through admitted broadcast IDs.
hypotheses.falsifier: Opaque-title empty-broadcast controls still answer source-bound questions at the same rate and with valid citations, or answer text appears in any pre-broadcast field.

hypotheses.claim: Visible titles preserve a covert answer channel, so the bottleneck is narrower but not closed.
hypotheses.falsifier: Informative-title versus randomized opaque-title controls produce invariant empty-broadcast accuracy and no source-bound details leak into generated directives.

hypotheses.claim: Removing excerpts blocks leakage but also deprives the contextual selector of evidence needed to distinguish relevant, conflicting and semi-relevant passages; lexical scores then become the actual selector.
hypotheses.falsifier: On held-out distractor/conflict pairs, title-and-score selection matches full-excerpt selector precision, entailment and conflict handling.

hypotheses.claim: Mechanical fallback converts model abstention into deterministic top-admitted broadcast, measuring gate throughput rather than GWT competition.
hypotheses.falsifier: Ablations show model-origin and mechanical-origin broadcasts have distinct logged arms and model selection adds reproducible answer-level value over admitted-top-k alone.

hypotheses.claim: MIN_GEDECKT=2 sharply rejects correct evidence when one discriminative term is enough, a synonym removes overlap, or evidence is causally/logically related rather than lexically duplicated.
hypotheses.falsifier: Human-labeled single-entity, paraphrase, causal and multi-hop probes show negligible additional gold-evidence rejection versus an evidential/semantic comparator.

hypotheses.claim: Raising excerpts to 1400 characters fixes one truncation boundary but still starves evidence located later in long articles.
hypotheses.falsifier: Position-swept probes with identical evidence at beginning/middle/end show invariant admission, materialization and answer correctness.

new_concepts.name: Selector-Generator Firewall
new_concepts.definition: The selector may identify evidence but cannot relay its answer-bearing content before the workspace gate.

new_concepts.name: Title Channel Leakage
new_concepts.definition: Metadata retained for selection contains enough semantic payload to answer without materialized evidence.

new_concepts.name: Blind Selector Paradox
new_concepts.definition: Closing content leakage removes the very evidence a semantic selector needs, causing a simpler scorer to become the de facto selector.

new_concepts.name: Selection Substitution
new_concepts.definition: A deterministic fallback replaces an abstaining contextual selector while downstream telemetry still observes a broadcast.

new_concepts.name: Two-Token Admission Cliff
new_concepts.definition: A hard minimum-overlap count creates a discontinuous false-rejection boundary unrelated to evidential sufficiency.

new_concepts.name: Position-Swept Sufficiency
new_concepts.definition: The same gold evidence is placed at controlled document positions to distinguish larger excerpts from genuinely sufficient evidence delivery.
